s: You feel the plain iron's honest weight and see rust waiting at the edges.
It is forged of good tempered steel, true and dependable.
p: They are forged of good tempered steel, true and dependable.

s: Silver runs through its make, and the restless dead fear its touch.
p: Silver runs through their make, and the restless dead fear its touch.

s: Elven smiths shaped it from a light, pale alloy of moonstone.
p: Elven smiths shaped them from a light, pale alloy of moonstone.

s: It is Dwemer work, made of a warm-coloured metal no rust can touch.
p: They are Dwemer work, made of a warm-coloured metal no rust can touch.

s: You feel how light the mithril is, though it outmatches any steel.
You feel adamantium's stubborn hardness: not even a scratch stays on it.
You see the black ebony drink in the light, cold and heavy in the hand.
Orcish smiths beat it out of dark, heavy orichalcum.
p: Orcish smiths beat them out of dark, heavy orichalcum.

s: You feel a faint, hungry heat rising from the daedric metal.
It is made of boiled and hardened leather.
p: They are made of boiled and hardened leather.

s: You see tightly linked rings, though their metal is impossible to name.
note: chain mail whose metal is not recorded (raw 256/259)

s: You feel the thick fur hold its warmth even in a biting wind.
It is made of tightly wound cloth.
p: They are made of tightly wound cloth.

s: You feel the interlocking rings shift with every movement of the body.
Metal plates riveted beneath the cloth make this a brigandine.
